channel.title: NBC Sports Rotoworld NFL Player News
channel.description: Unofficial personal Rotoworld NFL player-news feed.

item.title: Cowboys ruled out KaVontae Turpin (ribs) for Week 7 against the Eagles.
item.description:
KaVontae Turpin DAL Wide Receiver

Turpin’s absence will be felt most on special teams, with the team now forced to find a replacement on punt and kick returns. Otherwise, there is almost zero fantasy impact as the team’s WR4.

item.title: Falcons activated A.J. Terrell (groin) from injured reserve.
item.description:
A.J. Terrell ATL Cornerback

The Falcons have been attackable on the perimeter while playing most of the season without Terrell. Fellow cornerback C.J. Henderson is listed questionable for Week 7, but the reintegration of Terrell provides a much more difficult matchup for the injury-riddled 49ers.

item.title: Broncos activated Jonah Coleman (ankle) from injured reserve.
item.description:
Jonah Coleman DEN Running Back

Coleman missed the minimum four games as he tended to an ankle injury suffered in Week 2. He led the team in snaps in that contest and could return to the primary rushing role considering the inefficient play of J.K. Dobbins in his absence, making him worthy of a start in fantasy circles in a plus matchup against the Cardinals in his first game back.

item.title: Ravens ruled out Lamar Jackson (ankle) for Week 7 against the Bengals.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

Tyler Huntley will draw the start under center for the third straight game as Jackson continues to rehab a high-ankle sprain. Jackson reportedly took most of the first-team reps at practice Friday and was close to being able to play in Week 7, with the team ultimately siding with caution for their franchise quarterback. The Ravens enter a 15-game stretch in which they play three games starting in Week 8, which could have influenced their decision to hold Jackson out one more game. Expect him back for Week 8 against the Bills. His absence greatly influences the upside of the remaining skill position players considering Declan Doyle has halved his usage of play action and completely eliminated RPO with Huntley under center.

item.title: Dallas Goedert (knee) was removed from the injury report Saturday and will play against the Cowboys in Week 7.
item.description:
Dallas Goedert PHI Tight End

Goedert reportedly aggravated his previous knee injury but got back on the practice field for a full session Saturday before being removed from the injury report. He could be stepping into a massive target share with both DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks ruled out. Fantasy managers can start him as an upside TE1 in a great matchup against the Cowboys in Week 7.

item.title: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is questionable for Week 7 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

Although getting in a full practice Saturday, the Eagles head into Monday’s game against the Cowboys with Barkley listed as questionable following a two-game absence. Fantasy managers have a decision considering the Eagles play in Week 7’s final game on Monday Night Football, with no clear fall back options should he be unable to play. It would seem prudent to make alternate plans at the position.

item.title: Eagles ruled out DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) for Week 7 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

The Eagles will be without their top two receivers but got good news Saturday with the removal of Dallas Goedert from the injury report. Saquon Barkley is listed as questionable and appears to be a true game-time decision. Considering the low involvement of the backfield in the pass game this season, Goedert stands to benefit the most from the absences at wide receiver. He can be started as an upside TE1 in a solid on-paper matchup against the Cowboys.

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Vikings plan to activate Jordan Mason (thumb) from injured reserve.
item.description:
Jordan Mason MIN Running Back

Mason came into the season as the presumed lead back in a timeshare with Aaron Jones, the latter of whom has performed as a true workhorse in Mason’s absence. Although it could take a week or two for Mason to fully regain the lead back role, his presence significantly mutes the potential of Jones. Expect a near-even split when the Vikings take on the Colts in Week 7.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: Browns activated RB Dylan Sampson (knee) from injured reserve.
item.description:
Dylan Sampson CLE Running Back

Sampson was limited in practice throughout the week and listed as questionable for Week 7 against the Titans. Now that he’s officially been activated from injured reserve, he’s likely to be Cleveland’s change-of-pace back behind Quinshon Judkins this week. Sampson is worth stashing on fantasy benches, but is truly just a desperation FLEX play coming off a knee injury that’s sidelined him since Week 1.

Source: Fred Greetham

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that several teams believe the Jaguars could trade WR Brian Thomas Jr.
item.description:
Brian Thomas

Appearing on ESPN Saturday morning, Fowler, citing Thomas’ zero catches over the last two weeks, said something has to give in this situation. According to several teams the NFL Insider talked to, Thomas could be traded over the next few weeks. Fowler listed the Chiefs and Steelers as potentially interested teams and was emphatic that there will be suitors for Thomas. If you have Thomas in fantasy, it’s hard to imagine his value getting worse with a change of scenery. The Jaguars would appear content to roll with Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers and Travis Hunter as their top receivers in the event of a Thomas trade.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports “it’s more likely than not” that the Lions work out an extension with TE Sam LaPorta before free agency.
item.description:
Sam LaPorta DET Tight End

According to one of Jones’ sources, Lions GM Brad Holmes “does not like losing his draft picks, especially high ones.” A second-rounder in 2023, LaPorta made waves earlier this week when he expressed frustration with his lack of a contract extension on the Pardon My Take podcast. While those frustrations persist, the 25-year-old tight end clarified some of his comments to local Detroit media Friday, reiterating his desire to stay with the Lions long-term. Jones notes that other extensions the Lions have handed out have taken some time to get done. He also cautions that the team shouldn’t wait too long to sign LaPorta as the Raiders are unlikely to waste time making Brock Bowers the highest-paid tight end in football when he becomes extension-eligible after the season.

Source: Joanthan Jones

item.title: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports the Colts aren’t discussing a Jonathan Taylor trade yet.
item.description:
Jonathan Taylor IND Running Back

Jones writes that his understanding is the Colts will wait a few weeks before deciding what to do with their star running back. Indianapolis decided to move on from GM Chris Ballard after a 2-4 start. The way things are trending, it’s easy to imagine the Colts still on the outside of the playoff race in a few weeks. At that point interim GM Ed Dodds could look to recoup draft assets the team lost in previous trades. According to Jones, moving Taylor “would be the most expedient route” to acquiring a high draft pick. Citing sources, Jones lists the Giants and Vikings as potential suitors if Taylor is made available on the trade market. Taylor signed a two-year extension with the Colts in August that hasn’t even kicked in yet.

Source: Jonathan Jones

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Ravens QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) is “50/50" to play against the Bengals in Week 7.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

Appearing on ESPN Saturday morning, Fowler said the Ravens are “hopeful” that Jackson can play against the Bengals. He added that the team isn’t “overly optimistic” because, according to a source, Jackson is “50/50" to play in Week 7. If Jackson can’t go, Tyler Huntley will get the start and fantasy managers will need a backup plan this week. At this point, it’s unlikely we receive more clarity on the situation before inactives are released Sunday morning.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: Sam LaPorta said he wants to continue playing for the Lions long-term.
item.description:
Sam LaPorta DET Tight End

Earlier this week, LaPorta expressed frustration in an interview about his contract negotiations stalling in-season. The Athletic’s Colton Pouncy asked him a few follow-up questions today on the matter today, and LaPorta made clear that he hopes to remain a Lion long-term and is excited about the prospect of raising a family in Detroit. LaPorta seemed extremely earnest, saying he felt bad about his comments potentially causing a distraction for his team, but he knows his teammates care for him and want him to be happy and compensated. He handled the issue well and appears to be ready to play hard for a lucrative contract extension, which is good news for fantasy managers. LaPorta is a locked-in TE1 against the Packers this week.

Source: Colton Pouncy

item.title: Jevón Holland (concussion) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Texans.
item.description:
Jevón Holland NYG Safety

Holland, the Giants’ starting free safety, and Tyler Nubin (neck), the Giants’ starting strong safety, are both questionable to play. Meanwhile, starting perimeter CB Greg Newsome (concussion) has been ruled out. Expect the Texans’ passing offense to stay hot this week.

Source: New York Giants

item.title: Rashid Shaheed (hip) is not on the Seahawks’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Rashid Shaheed SEA Wide Receiver

The Seahawks’ sporadic producer will be on the field against the Chiefs this week. Shaheed has been involved as a receiver and as a rusher, scoring touchdowns in consecutive weeks. He offers a low floor, but he makes for a viable FLEX starter this week.

Source: Seattle Seahawks

item.title: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Steelers.
item.description:
CJ Donaldson NO Running Back

Donaldson is the third member of the Saints’ backfield committee. While he will get a few touches this week, he is not getting enough work for fantasy relevance.

Source: New Orleans Saints

item.title: Landon Dickerson (knee/pectoral) was limited on Friday.
item.description:
Landon Dickerson PHI Guard

Dickerson injured a pectoral muscle on Thursday, complicating his knee-related return from injured reserve. He is firmly in the questionable camp at this time. Eagles C Drew Kendall (knee) was upgraded to full participation.

Source: Jeff McLane

item.title: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) was limited on Friday.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

We had really hoped to see Barkley practice in full today. He still has a chance to take the field when the Eagles face the Cowboys in Week 7’s Monday Night Football game, but he is inching toward a questionable designation right now. Upgrading to full tomorrow would increase his odds of playing.

Source: Jeff McLane

item.title: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) did not practice on Friday.
item.description:
Dontayvion Wicks PHI Wide Receiver

Wicks has been banged up for weeks, and the Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane said Wicks might miss the Eagles’ Week 7 game against the Cowboys. Hopefully, he resumes practicing tomorrow. Stay tuned.

Source: Jeff McLane

item.title: Dallas Goedert (knee) did not practice on Friday.
item.description:
Dallas Goedert PHI Tight End

Goedert is on the wrong side of questionable for the Eagles’ Week 7 Monday Night Football game against the Cowboys. The Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane reports that as of Thursday, there was “optimism” about Goedert’s Week 7 availability. Hopefully, he resumes practicing tomorrow.

Source: Jeff McLane

item.title: The Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane said he got “the sense” that DeVonta Smith (hamstring) will not play in Week 7 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

Like Thursday, Smith was sidelined for Friday’s practice. The Eagles have been managing his practice reps and pulled him out for multiple drives in their Week 6 loss to the Panthers. The Eagles face the Cowboys on Monday night, giving Smith an extra day to rest. Consider him highly questionable to play at this time. McLane adds that Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) could also sit out this week.

Source: Jeff McLane

item.title: Kendal Daniels (neck) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the 49ers.
item.description:
Kendal Daniels ATL Linebacker

Daniels was taken off the field on a stretcher last week, but managed to practice in full to begin the week. Daniels, a rookie, has 23 tackles, three quarterback pressures and one sack this season.

Source: Atlanta Falcons

item.title: A.J. Terrell (groin) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the 49ers.
item.description:
A.J. Terrell ATL Cornerback

Both Terrell and CB C.J. Henderson (groin) are questionable to play after practicing in full on Friday. Getting them back in the starting lineup would be very helpful for the Falcons’ defense.

Source: Atlanta Falcons

item.title: Budda Baker (groin/illness) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Budda Baker ARI Safety

Baker practiced in a limited capacity on Friday, and the veteran safety is no stranger to playing through injuries. The Cardinals ruled out DL Walter Nolen (ankle) and S Andrew Wingard (knee). Cardinals CB Garrett Williams (knee) has been cleared to play.

Source: Darren Urban

item.title: Broncos ruled out Jonah Elliss (ankle) for Week 7 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Jonah Elliss DEN Linebacker

Reporting from earlier this week indicates Ellis could be sidelined for a few weeks. Broncos S Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) was also ruled out this week.

Source: Denver Broncos

item.title: Pat Surtain (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Pat Surtain DEN Cornerback

Surtain never managed to practice in full this week. Keeping him sidelined until he is able to do so could make sense. The 4-2 Broncos are currently second in the AFC West. They face the 5-0 Chiefs in Week 8. Stay tuned.

Source: Denver Broncos

item.title: Jonah Coleman (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Jonah Coleman DEN Running Back

Coleman practiced in full all week, but the Broncos could technically give him another week to rehab the ankle. If active, there are too many unknowns regarding Coleman’s potential workload to start him in the FLEX, but he must be rostered in 12-team leagues.

Source: Denver Broncos

item.title: Broncos ruled out Tyler Badie (thumb) for Week 7
item.description:
Tyler Badie DEN Running Back

Badie is likely headed toward a demotion with Jonah Coleman (ankle) inching toward a return. The latter player is questionable to play this week.

Source: Denver Broncos

item.title: Jaylen Waddle (chest) is not on the Broncos’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Jaylen Waddle DEN Wide Receiver

Waddle upgraded to full on Friday after logging two limited sessions to begin the week. The Broncos’ No. 1 wide receiver has struggled to deliver usable stat lines with Bo Nix intent on checking down. The Cardinals’ pass defense could facilitate a bounce-back game for Waddle, but he remains a WR3/FLEX at this time.

Source: Denver Broncos

item.title: Drew Lock (right elbow) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Drew Lock SEA Quarterback

The Seahawks’ backup quarterback is dealing with an injury in his throwing arm, so any calls for Sam Darnold’s benching will have to quiet down. Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori (hip), LB DeMarcus Lawrence (knee) and LB Uchenna Nwosu (hip) are questionable. The Seahawks ruled out Chazz Surratt (calf) and LB DrakeThomas (ankle).

Source: Andrew Destin

item.title: Vikings released RB Deejay Dallas.
item.description:
DeeJay Dallas MIN Running Back

He’ll likely find his way back to the practice squad — here or elsewhere — at some point this season. This move portends that Jordan Mason will be activated for Week 7.

item.title: Christian Kirk (calf) is questionable for San Francisco’s Week 7 game against the Falcons.
item.description:
Christian Kirk SF Wide Receiver

We’ve heard worse desperation options than “most accomplished 49ers wideout on paper playing with Brock Purdy and George Kittle as Mike Evans sits.” Kirk probably factors in the WR3/WR4 calculus after being activated from injured reserve Saturday.

item.title: Nick Bosa (calf) will not play in San Francisco’s Week 7 game against the Falcons.
item.description:
Nick Bosa SF Defensive Lineman

The 49ers keep projecting a rosy picture of Bosa returning to practice at some point, it keeps not happening. He’ll get the Week 8 bye to heal up. Bosa hasn’t played since Week 2. If only there were a reserve list that teams could place injured players on.

item.title: Seahawks ruled out Zach Charbonnet (knee) for Week 7 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Zach Charbonnet SEA Running Back

Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald told reporters that Charbonnet has not suffered a setback. He just isn’t ready yet. Many teams might rush a player of his caliber back, now that he is practicing in full, but the Seahawks are smartly taking the long view with Charbonnet’s health. Emanuel Wilson will function as the team’s leading rusher while George Holani plays on passing downs.

Source: Andrew Destin

item.title: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) won’t play in San Francisco’s Week 7 game against the Falcons.
item.description:
Deebo Samuel SF Wide Receiver

Samuel hasn’t practiced since injuring his hamstring in the latter stages of Week 5’s win over the Seahawks. He’ll get the Week 8 bye to heal up. It does seem like there’s at least some chance he could get active for Week 9.

item.title: Mike Evans (Achilles) will not play in San Francisco’s Week 7 game against the Falcons.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

He didn’t practice all week and will get San Francisco’s Week 8 bye to recover. The 33-year-old’s absence will leave veterans Christian Kirk and Brandin Cooks along with youngsters Jacob Cowing and Jordan Watkins on the 49ers receiver depth chart for Sunday.

item.title: Tyler Guyton (calf) practiced in full on Friday.
item.description:
Tyler Guyton DAL Tackle

This is great news for the Cowboys’ offense. Guyton, the starting left tackle, is practicing in full and still has another practice tomorrow. Expect him to be available for the Cowboys’ Monday Night Football game against the Eagles.

Source: Adam Caplan

item.title: Trent Brown (wrist) is not on Houston’s final Week 7 injury report.
item.description:
Trent Brown HOU Tackle

He’ll be good to go after back-to-back full sessions on Thursday and Friday. The 380-pound behemoth will likely continue to spend plenty of time on the injury report in his age-33 season.

item.title: Dalton Schultz (quad) is not on Houston’s final Week 7 injury report.
item.description:
Dalton Schultz HOU Tight End

He’ll be good to go, but given how much Houston’s wideout usage has expanded of late, Schultz is probably just a passable TE2.

item.title: George Pickens (shoulder) said he will play in Week 7 against the Eagles.
item.description:
George Pickens DAL Wide Receiver

The Cowboys face the Eagles in Week 7’s Monday Night Football game, giving Pickens an extra day to recover. ESPN’s Todd Archer said yesterday that Pickens has been icing his shoulder in-game during the Cowboys’ last two games. He encouragingly practiced in full today. Start him as a WR2 as usual this week.

Source: Jon Machota

item.title: Matthew Golden (shoulder) is not on the Packers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Lions.
item.description:
Matthew Golden GB Wide Receiver

A few Packers got a little banged up against the Cowboys last week, including Golden, but the breakout second-year wide receiver is good to go. This game profiles as a fantasy-friendly shootout. Golden should be started as a high-end WR2 with solid upside.

Source: Rob Demovsky

item.title: Brock Bowers (hamstring/calf) is not on Las Vegas’ final Week 7 injury report.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

A Friday afternoon tradition unlike any other, Bowers was cleared after getting in two full sessions on Thursday and Friday. He can be played as an elite TE1, as usual.

item.title: Christian Watson (ankle) is not on the Packers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Lions.
item.description:
Christian Watson GB Wide Receiver

Watson remained limited through the first two practices this week. We do not yet know his Friday participation level, but he seems to be ready for action. Watson belongs in the WR1 tier against a Lions’ pass defense that has freely surrendered big plays this season.

Source: Rob Demovsky

item.title: Jordan Love (back) is not on the Packers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Lions.
item.description:
Jordan Love GB Quarterback

Love was limited on Wednesday before upgrading to full on Thursday. Packers coach Matt LaFleur told reporters that his starting quarterback was “pretty beat up” after the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys. Hopefully, he is feeling much better by now. This divisional showdown looks like one of the most fantasy-friendly game environments in Week 7. He’s a QB1.

Source: Rob Demovsky

item.title: The Athletic’s Dan Duggan reports Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder) will miss the remainder of the season.
item.description:
Tremaine Edmunds NYG Linebacker

Edmunds will presumably be placed on IR before Week 7’s game against the Texans. He managed a 52.0 PFF grade in 380 snaps over six games, recording two sacks and 50 combined tackles. Edmunds will enter year two of his three-year deal with the Giants in 2027, in what will be his age-29 season.

Source: Dan Duggan

item.title: Theo Johnson (neck) is doubtful for Week 7 against the Texans.
item.description:
Theo Johnson NYG Tight End

Johnson is not fantasy-relevant on his own, but he can help out the Giants’ offense in real life when he is available. Isaiah Likely is the Giants’ clear-cut TE1.

Source: Dan Salomone

item.title: Andrew Thomas (groin) is not on the Giants’ final injury report for Week 7 against the Texans.
item.description:
Andrew Thomas NYG Tackle

Thomas has played through injuries in multiple games this year. Giants RT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) and backup OT Marcus Mbow (knee) both resumed practicing in a limited capacity on Thursday and are officially questionable to play this week. The Texans’ defense has underperformed this year. Perhaps this is a get-right matchup for them.

Source: Art Stapleton

item.title: Brian Branch (Achilles) is questionable for Detroit’s Week 7 game against the Packers.
item.description:
Brian Branch DET Defensive Back

After three full sessions this week, Branch is expected to be activated off reserve/PUP and should have no snap count per DC Kelvin Sheppard. He can be welcomed back to IDP lineups.

item.title: Cade Mays (wrist) is questionable for Detroit’s Week 7 game against the Packers.
item.description:
Cade Mays DET Center

Questionable but fully expected to play after three full practices, Mays should add some more teeth to the Lions’ run game.

item.title: The Athletic’s Dan Duggan believes Cam Skattebo “will be back in the mix” in Week 7 against the Texans, likely in “some sort of timeshare with Tyrone Tracy and Devin Singletary.”
item.description:
Cam Skattebo NYG Running Back

Sigh. Three-player backfields are generally fantasy-unfriendly situations, and this one is no different. Skattebo is a capable dual-threat player who has seemingly been limited by the significant ankle injury he suffered last year. The Giants could get him more involved in the passing game, but Tracy can contribute there as well, muddying that opportunity. Singletary would not be a contributor for many NFL teams, but lucky him, he’s a New York Giant. Skattebo and Tracy are viable FLEX options, though both are likely touchdown-dependent.

Source: Dan Duggan

item.title: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 7 injury report.
item.description:
Rashod Bateman BAL Wide Receiver

He practiced in full twice on Thursday and Friday. With Ja’Kobi Lane eating into his targets and the Bengals ever-vulnerable through the air by tight ends, Bateman is probably only a deep-league play in Week 7.

item.title: Travis Kelce (ankle) is not on Kansas City’s final Week 7 injury report.
item.description:
Travis Kelce KC Tight End

He’ll be a reliable TE1, even in a tough matchup against Seattle’s defense, as the Chiefs simply don’t have many other Trusted Mahomes Targets healthy for this one. It’s essentially just Kelce and Xavier Worthy healthy of Kansas City’s main targets.

item.title: Tyjae Spears (knee) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 7 game against the Browns.
item.description:
Tyjae Spears TEN Running Back

Spears has been active off a questionable line twice since Week 4. We’d imagine he’d get there again after a limited Friday session. The touch upside just isn’t there for him to be more than a deep-league FLEX play at this point.

item.title: Baker Mayfield (thumb) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles told reporters earlier today that Mayfield “looks like he’s ready to go” for this week’s game. Mayfield seemingly has solid odds of suiting up this week, but we must wait for an official ruling. Hopefully, that arrives tomorrow. If active, Mayfield will play with a protective plate on the back of his glove to help keep his recently dislocated thumb in place. He is a QB2 for the occasion, if active.

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: Calvin Ridley (hip) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 7 game against the Browns.
item.description:
Calvin Ridley TEN Wide Receiver

He didn’t practice Thursday or Friday, and we’d consider him on the pessimistic side of questionable. Not that you were thinking about playing him anyway.

item.title: Bucky Irving (illness) is not on the Buccaneers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Bucky Irving TB Running Back

As is typically the case with ill players, Irving is good to go for this week’s game. He upgraded to full participation today after getting a limited session in on Thursday. The Buccaneers’ No. 1 running back has been a volatile producer this season, yet even with last week’s flop, he still totaled 21 touches. That type of workload keeps him firmly in the RB2 ranks.

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: Ashton Dulin (hamstring) is not on Indianapolis’ final Week 7 injury report.
item.description:
Ashton Dulin IND Wide Receiver

With Tyler Warren down, Dulin probably figures to join Keenan Allen and Josh Downs as one of Indianapolis’ three main receivers. He has some desperation play viability in deeper leagues.

item.title: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Bam Knight will handle “a lot of work” on early downs with Jeremiyah Love (ankle) sidelined.
item.description:
Zonovan Knight ARI Running Back

LaFleur simply does not believe that any one running back can handle a full-time role and remain healthy, so he employs a committee approach. Although Tyler Allgeier sits ahead of Knight on the depth chart, LaFleur said he views Allgeier as a reliable complementary running back who excels in pass protection and short-yardage. Knight will be the team’s lead rusher on early downs and can be started in the FLEX against the Broncos this week.

Source: Tyler Drake

item.title: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Tyler Allgeier is “always” going to serve as a complementary running back.
item.description:
Tyler Allgeier ARI Running Back

LaFleur really laid it all out there at today’s press conference, saying Allgeier “is always going to complement that next guy” when the starter is out. He adds that Allgeier is “extremely smart” and can be trusted in pass protection and short-yardage situations on third down. While Allgeier “can” do what the Cardinals need him to do on first and second down, LaFleur said Bam Knight will take “a lot” of that work with Jeremiyah Love (ankle) sidelined. LaFleur closed by saying he does not think any of these running backs can hold up in a full-time role over the course of the season. Allgeier handled a hefty 19 touches in this complementary role last week. He can be started as a high-volume FLEX with touchdown-based upside against the Broncos.

Source: Tyler Drake

item.title: Christian Kirk (calf) is questionable for San Francisco’s Week 7 game against the Falcons.
item.description:
Christian Kirk SF Wide Receiver

He is, however, expected to be activated off injured reserve and play. We’ve heard worse desperation options than “most accomplished 49ers wideout on paper playing with Brock Purdy and George Kittle as Mike Evans sits.” Kirk probably factors in the WR3/WR4 calculus assuming he is indeed activated on Saturday.

item.title: GeorgePickens (shoulder) said he will play in Week 7 against the Eagles.
item.description:
George Pickens DAL Wide Receiver

The Cowboys face the Eagles in Week 7’s Monday Night Football game, giving Pickens an extra day to recover. ESPN’s Todd Archer said yesterday that Pickens has been icing his shoulder in-game during the Cowboys’ last two games. He encouragingly practiced in full today. Start him as a WR2 as usual this week.

Source: Jon Machota

item.title: Mike Washington (foot/back) is questionable for Las Vegas’ Week 7 game against the Rams.
item.description:
Mike Washington Jr. LV Running Back

Washington didn’t practice on Thursday and was not spotted at practice on Friday. It would seem that he’s a very tenuous questionable at this point. Dylan Laube would be next up for backup duties behind Ashton Jeanty if Washington were ruled out.

Source: Sam Warren

item.title: Trent McDuffie (groin) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Trent McDuffie

McDuffie has not practiced since straining his groin in Week 6’s Thursday practice. Labeling him as questionable to play seems like a formality before a game-day inactive listing, but only the Rams’ staffers know for sure. The Rams ruled out LB Nate Landman (concussion). Practice squad LB Eric Kendricks will be promoted to the active roster for Week 7.

Source: Nate Atkins

item.title: Puka Nacua (calf) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

The fact that Nacua is not practicing today is a bad sign for his Week 7 availability. Ever the injury-related optimist, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported earlier today that Nacua’s injury is “more minor than anything else,” though he quickly balanced the scales by then saying that he would not call Nacua’s quick trip to the imaging room “precautionary, because it’s not nothing.” If active, Nacua should be in fantasy football lineups because his talent and workload are almost unparalleled. Unfortunately, coach Sean McVay told reporters that Nacua felt that “he wasn’t able to have some of the power and full explosion.” Nacua is on the wrong side of questionable, and the Rams obviously do not want his injury to worsen.

Source: Sarah Barshop

item.title: Brashard Smith (hamstring) won’t play in Kansas City’s Week 7 game against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Brashard Smith KC Running Back

Did you remember he was on the roster? Funny what one little Kenneth Walker signing will do. Smith has one touch and six snaps in five games. Jadyn Ott will get RB3 duties in Week 7.

item.title: T.J. Hockenson (concussion) is not on the Vikings’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Colts.
item.description:
T.J. Hockenson MIN Tight End

Hockenson suffered a concussion in Week 5 against the Saints and was able to heal up over the Vikings’ Week 6. He demonstrated a solid connection with Kyler Murray in Week 4, posting a 13/119 receiving line against the Dolphins. Hockenson can be treated as a TE1 this week against the Colts.

Source: Alec Lewis

item.title: Rashee Rice (hamstring) will not play in Kansas City’s Week 7 game against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Rashee Rice KC Wide Receiver

Rice didn’t practice all week despite Andy Reid’s optimistic spin that he’s a “quick healer.” It’s hard to make much sense of how available he’ll be for Week 8 at this point as Rice hasn’t practiced since before the team’s Week 5 bye. Xavier Worthy will again get a WR3-caliber workload as The Only Game In Town for the Chiefs wideouts.

Source: Nate Taylor

item.title: Justin Jefferson (ankle) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Colts.
item.description:
Justin Jefferson MIN Wide Receiver

Coming off the Vikings’ Week 6 bye, Jefferson got in a limited session on Wednesday before returning to full participation on Thursday. The star wide receiver posted a 6/79/1 receiving line in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints. He should be treated as an elite WR1 against a Colts pass defense that will be without CB Sauce Gardner (calf).

Source: Alec Lewis

item.title: Bears coach Ben Johnson said Cole Kmet (knee) will miss the rest of the season.
item.description:
Cole Kmet CHI Tight End

Unfortunately it’s not much of a surprise based on the reporting or the carting. Sam Roush will take over as Chicago’s TE2 and likely have fringe TE2 value. Kmet will be in the final year of his four-year, $50 million extension in 2027. The 28-year-old will be a potential cap casualty with a $15.425 million cap figure and $10 million in savings on release without getting into post-June 1 cap machinations.

Source: Phillip Thompson

item.title: Jordan Mason (thumb) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Colts.
item.description:
Jordan Mason MIN Running Back

Mason practiced in full all week. He seemingly has good odds of suiting up, but sometimes NFL teams will give players extra time off when they are returning from injured reserve. If Mason plays this weekend, he should be able to handle his normal lead-rushing role. In that case, he can be started as an RB2/FLEX.

Source: Alec Lewis

item.title: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Carson Beck is dealing with back spasms.
item.description:
Carson Beck ARI Quarterback

Beck left Thursday’s practice with back spasms and was listed as a DNP. Head coach Mike LaFleur said he was not overly concerned about the injury and that he doesn’t believe it will be anything long-term. Beck’s injury shouldn’t change his Week 7 availability, as he has been the emergency QB3 all season. He was officially listed as questionable to play.

item.title: Lamar Jackson (ankle) said he’s “heading in the right direction” when asked if he’d play in Week 7.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

Here’s what happened: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter spoke and said the team is still “working through” whether Jackson would play on Sunday, and then the team took the unusual step of having both Jackson and Tyler Huntley talk to the media. Jackson also said he doesn’t need to be 100% to play and clarified that he had a high-ankle sprain. Jackson officially draw a questionable tag after a limited Friday session. Reading between the lines, the fact that Huntley spoke probably sets us up nicely for a rug pull, but Jackson-reliant fantasy managers will probably be waiting until inactives on Sunday before they know for sure.

Source: Jamison Hensley

item.title: Denzel Ward (hand) was limited in Friday’s practice and is questionable for Cleveland’s Week 7 game against the Titans.
item.description:
Denzel Ward CLE Cornerback

Ward popped up on the injury report today. Friday pop-up questionables are always tough to understand from the outside without any major reporting, but it stands to reason that Ward has a real chance to miss the game based on the listing. The Browns cleared Carson Schwesinger (ankle) from the report, so at least their star linebacker will be in there.

item.title: Denzel Boston (foot) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 7 injury report.
item.description:
Denzel Boston CLE Wide Receiver

He’ll be on the WR3 line in a good matchup against the Titans. Boston finally had a clunker last week against Baltimore, but he’s been remarkably consistent otherwise and should find easier footing against Tennessee’s rough back seven.

item.title: KC Concepcion (calf/quad) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 7 injury report.
item.description:
KC Concepcion KC Concepcion (calf/quad) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 7 injury report.

Concepcion should be treated as a PPR WR3/WR4 tweener this week in a good matchup against the Titans. With Denzel Boston also active, we likely won’t be seeing any major explosions here. Concepcion-reliant managers would accept any explosion at this point as he’s found it hard to crack 50 receiving yards so far.
item.rw:position: Concepcion (calf/quad) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 7 injury report.

item.title: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Carson Beck is dealing with back spasms.
item.description:
Carson Beck ARI Quarterback

Beck left Thursday’s practice with back spasms and was listed as a DNP. Head coach Mike LaFleur said he was not overly concerned with the injury and that he doesn’t believe it will be anything long-term. Beck’s injury shouldn’t change his Week 7 availability, as he has been the emergency QB3 all season.

item.title: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 7 injury report.
item.description:
Quinshon Judkins CLE Running Back

He should carry his usual load in a good matchup against the Titans. That will put Judkins in the mid-to-low RB2 range this week, even with Dylan Sampson getting a chance to come back off injured reserve.

item.title: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will not play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Jeremiyah Love ARI Running Back

Things have been trending in this direction all week, but LaFleur officially confirmed on Friday that Love will miss a second straight game. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will likely split duties again in Week 7 after seeing a near 50/50 split in the touch distribution last week, with Allgeier’s 19 touches narrowly edging out Knight’s 17. Both Allgeier and Knight are fringe RB2/RB3 plays against a stout Broncos defense. In addition to Love the Cardinals also ruled out DT Walter Nolen III (ankle), S Andrew Wiggins (ankle), and OG Jo Gaines II (ankle).

Source: Josh Weinfuss

item.title: Dylan Sampson (knee/IR) is questionable for Cleveland’s Week 7 game against the Titans.
item.description:
Dylan Sampson CLE Running Back

If active, he will be a change-up back for Quinshon Judkins, who is not carrying a status this week. Coming off a long-term injury, it would be a real leap of faith to put Sampson in a FLEX role this week, even against the Titans.

item.title: Divine Deablo (forearm) won’t play in Atlanta’s Week 7 game against the 49ers.
item.description:
Divine Deablo ATL Linebacker

It’s a slight upgrade for Christian McCaffrey, not that you were thinking about not starting McCaffrey anyway. The Falcons also ruled out CB Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring) — neither player practiced this week.

item.title: Buccaneers ruled out Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) for Week 7 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Emeka Egbuka TB Wide Receiver

Just minutes after head coach Todd Bowles said the team would list Egbuka as doubtful, the official injury report listed him as out, despite his limited participation in Friday’s practice. Egbuka was unable to clear concussion protocol in time to be active for this week, and will now set his sights on returning in Week 8 in time to face the Falcons.

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) won’t play in Atlanta’s Week 7 game against the 49ers.
item.description:
Brian Robinson ATL Running Back

Bijan should get a larger-than-usual workload this week against San Francisco. The Falcons only have two running backs on the 53-man roster so it may be Khalil Herbert or Jam Miller filling in as (Bijan) Robinson’s backup on Sunday. Herbert seems like the logical choice.

item.title: Sauce Gardner (calf) will not play in Week 7 against the Vikings.
item.description:
Sauce Gardner IND Cornerback

Gardner was never expected to play this week after it was announced on Monday that he would be week-to-week with his calf injury. His absence could be a good sign for Vikings pass-catchers this week in what should be a plus matchup against a Colts defense that ranks 14th in fantasy points allowed to receivers this season. In addition to Gardner, the Colts also ruled out WR Anthony Gould (concussion).

Source: Stephen Holder

item.title: Tyler Warren (groin) will not play in Week 7 against the Vikings.
item.description:
Tyler Warren IND Tight End

Warren was a DNP throughout the week and has now been ruled out for this week’s game against the Vikings. This will be the second straight missed game for Warren, who first suffered the injury in last Friday’s practice. The Vikings have allowed the fewest fantasy points to opposing tight ends this season, meaning fantasy managers are best off avoiding Will Mallory and Mo Alie-Cox as streaming options this week.

Source: Stephen Holder

item.title: Buccaneers head coach said Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) will be doubtful for Week 7’s game against the Panthers.
item.description:
Emeka Egbuka TB Wide Receiver

Bowles said Egbuka remains in concussion protocol and initially said “I’d say he’s out [for Week 7], too,” before saying the second-year receiver would be listed as doubtful. Fantasy managers holding out hope that Egbuka will suit up for Sunday’s game against the Panthers should ensure their backup plan is in place, as players listed as doubtful seldom end up playing on game day. Assuming he’s out, Ted Hurst could be tasked with operating as the Bucs’ WR1. Hurst has caught 11-of-22 targets for 168 yards and one touchdown this season but wouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a WR3/FLEX play even with Baker Mayfield (thumb) back under center.

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Baker Mayfield (thumb) “looks like he’s ready to go” for Week 7 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

Mayfield was a full participant in practice all week and should be removed from the team’s final injury report when it’s released later in the day. Mayfield is expected to wear a protective glove on his throwing hand, which should prevent injury to the thumb he dislocated in Week 3, and will be on the QB2 radar in what is a must-win game for the 1-5 Buccaneers. Hopefully he can improve on a rough start to the season in which he threw for 615-2-2 in his first three games while completing 63.5 percent of his passes.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Lamar Jackson (ankle) was spotted at practice on Friday.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

This makes three straight practices for Jackson, who continues to trend in the right direction ahead of Week 7’s game against the Bengals. Jackson was listed as a limited participant in each of the first two practices to start the week and should have a good chance of suiting up, even if he’s only listed as a limited participant. We will provide an update on his official status when the team announces it, but this is yet another encouraging sign for the two-time MVP.

Source: Baltimore Ravens

item.title: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Josh Jacobs is on track to play in Week 7 against the Lions.
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

LaFleur said Jacobs’ Week 7 status depends on how he gets through Friday’s practice. The 28-year-old back has looked “great” in practice this week, per an earlier quote from OC Adam Stenavich, and seems to be trending toward a return after a six-week stay on the Commissioner’s Exempt List. At this point, we would be surprised if Jacobs didn’t play this week against the Lions, but it’s too early to assume he will see his normal workload in his first game back. Even if he doesn’t get a full assortment of touches, we would still expect Jacobs to get enough work to justify starting him at RB2.

Source: Rob Demovsky

item.title: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports David Montgomery (groin) will not play in Week 7 against the Giants.
item.description:
David Montgomery HOU Running Back

This will be the second game in a row that Montgomery has missed due to the groin injury he suffered in Week 5. Woody Marks, who totaled 17 touches in last week’s win over the Jaguars will again lead the Texans’ backfield. He has averaged 18.0 touches per game over the last two weeks and will be a volume-based RB2 with a chance at significant upside. Safeties Jalen Pitre (AC joint) and S Reed Blankenship (concussion) will also miss this week’s game against the Giants, putting the Texans down a handful of starters with one game left before their Week 8 bye.

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) was seen practicing on Friday.
item.description:
Emeka Egbuka TB Wide Receiver

Egbuka missed the first two practices of the week, but could have a shot at suiting up after appearing on the practice field Friday. Head coach Todd Bowles should give an update on Egbuka shortly after practice, so we’ll check back on his official status once we have word on his Week 7 availability. Whether or not he has a chance to play will largely depend on the team’s independent neurologists clearing him from the league’s concussion protocol.

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Adonai Mitchell (finger) will play in Week 7 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Adonai Mitchell NYJ Wide Receiver

Mitchell has been sidelined since injuring his finger in preparation for the Jets’ Week 3 game against the Lions. It was incredibly unfortunate time for Mitchell and his fantasy managers, as his injury came just days after he went for 6-63-0 on 12 targets against the Packers. Mitchell’s return could complicate things for Omar Cooper’s fantasy managers after Cooper broke out for 6-103-1 against the Patriots last week. The Jets rank 13th in the league in plays run from 11-personnel (209) through the first six weeks of the season, which means both Mitchell and Cooper should see plenty of snaps. That said, neither player should be viewed as anything more than a WR3/FLEX play until we see how the target distribution looks with both players active.

Source: New York Jets

item.title: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) will be questionable for Week 7 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Breece Hall NYJ Running Back

Glenn said Hall will be limited in Friday’s practice and that the team will “see how that goes” to close out the week. Hall has missed the last three games with his quad injury but the fact he is closing out the week with two-straight limited practices suggests he’ll be a true game-time decision entering Sunday. If he’s unable to play, Braelon Allen would again serve as the primary back in the Jets’ backfield and would be a fringe RB1/RB2 in what is shaping up to be a plus matchup against the lowly Dolphins.

Source: New York Jets

item.title: Jaylen Wright (foot) will play in Week 7 against the Jets.
item.description:
Jaylen Wright MIA Running Back

Wright has rushed 14 times for 28 scoreless yards this season and has yet to receive a target in the four games he has appeared in. Fellow running back Ollie Gordon has emerged as the unquestioned RB1 for the Dolphins since the team lost De’Von Achane (knee) in Week 3. Wright is well off the fantasy radar at this point.

Source: Barry Jackson

item.title: Dolphins WR Caleb Douglas (ankle) will play in Week 7 against the Jets.
item.description:
Caleb Douglas MIA Wide Receiver

Douglas hasn’t played since Week 2 against the 49ers, but the rookie caught five passes for 94 yards in his pro debut against the Raiders and has been targeted on 16.4 percent of his routes. Stuck in a Dolphins offense that currently ranks 31st in scoring and passing yards, Douglas will be hard to trust as anything more than a fringe WR3/WR4 this week against a top-five Jets pass defense.

Source: Marcel Louis-Jacques

item.title: T.J. Watt (calf) was removed from the Steelers’ Week 7 injury report and will play against the Saints.
item.description:
T.J. Watt PIT Linebacker

Watt popped up on Thursday’s injury report with a calf injury and was listed as limited. On Friday, he was upgraded to a full participant in what was an estimated report, but he does not carry an injury status heading into the weekend. S DeShon Elliott (knee) is listed as questionable but was listed as a full participant throughout the week.

Source: Mike Triplett

item.title: Alvin Kamara (back) was removed from the injury report for Week 7’s game against the Steelers.
item.description:
Alvin Kamara NO Running Back

Kamara was still listed as limited in Friday’s practice, but the Saints feel confident enough in his health to clear him for Week 7. Kamara found the end zone last week on a 31-yard reception, but has largely been inefficient with his touches this season. He seen 14 opportunities to Kendre Miller’s 30 over the last two weeks and will be hard to trust as anything more than a touchdown-dependent RB3 against the Steelers. The only players on the Saints carrying injury designations into the weekend are guard Cesar Ruiz (knee) and DL Nathan Sheperd (illness). Both are listed as questionable.

Source: New Orleans Saints

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Puka Nacua’s calf injury is not considered “a significant injury.”
item.description:
Puka Nacua

As far as Nacua’s long-term status goes, this sounds like good news overall. However, Rapoport also noted that Nacua’s status for Sunday’s game against the Raiders could be “up in the air.” With Friday’s practice still to go, Nacua’s status will be one to look for later in the day, as will his designation entering the weekend. If he draws a questionable tag, fantasy managers should treat him as a true game-day decision and have a backup plan in place should be unable to play this week. Given the 4:25 PM EST start time for this game, Rams WR Konata Mumpfield could be on a short list of players worth stashing until we know more about Nacua’s availability.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: FOX59’s Tyler Haughn reports Colts QB Anthony Richardson was charged with misdemeanor possession of marijuana earlier this week.
item.description:
Anthony Richardson IND Quarterback

According to reports, Richardson was stopped on October 12th for having a registration on his car that had expired and was assigned to a different vehicle. The officer reported noticing the “odor of marijuana” coming from Richardson’s car, and the former first-round pick admitted to smoking in the car; a “small mason jar containing a substance believed to be marijuana and an opened bag of THC-infused gummies” were found in his vehicle during a search. Richardson is scheduled to have a bench trial on January 4th, 2027. While the NFL no longer suspends players for testing positive for THC, it’s possible Richardson faces some kind of penalty from the league with this being a legal issue.

Source: FOX59

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Cole Kmet will undergo additional tests on his knee after Week 7’s win over the Patriots.
item.description:
Cole Kmet CHI Tight End

Head coach Ben Johnson said after the game that Kmet’s injury didn’t look “very good,” breaking from his normal tendency to avoid talking about injuries. Kmet’s knee buckled from under him in the fourth quarter of Thursday’s game, and he had to be carted from the field after the play. This looked like a potential season-ender when it happened, but tests will confirm the severity of it in the near future. Kmet’s absence could open up more opportunities for Colston Loveland, who has caught 26 passes for 244 yards and two touchdowns this season.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Rico Dowdle (knee) is questionable for Week 7 against the Saints.
item.description:
Rico Dowdle PIT Running Back

Dowdle was listed as limited throughout the week and will officially be questionable entering this week’s game with the Saints. This is a new injury he is dealing with but it doesn’t sound like he’s at serious risk of missing the game at this time. Dowdle played on just 17 percent of snaps in his return to action last week and saw 11 opportunities. He’ll profile as a low-end RB3 this week if active.

Source: Brooke Pryor

item.title: Jaguars OL Anton Harrison was revealed to have a torn ACL, ending his season.
item.description:
Anton Harrison

Surgeons discovered Harrison suffered a torn ACL while performing knee surgery on him Thursday. The 23-year-old lineman will now be placed on season-ending IR, with hopes of returning in time for training camp next season. Harrison allowed just 13 pressures and two sacks in five games this season, earning a PFF pass-blocking grade of 67.2. Walker Little, who took over in Harrison’s absence, started last week against the Texans and will assume the starting left tackle role going forward.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Rome Odunze caught 4-of-5 targets for 69 yards in the Bears’ Week 7 win over the Patriots.
item.description:
Rome Odunze CHI Wide Receiver

The yardage total goes down as Odunze’s second highest mark of the season as the third-year receiver was held out of the end zone for the seventh straight game to start the 2026 season. He did make three massive catches on third downs to help extend drives, making his mark felt more with quality than quantity. That doesn’t necessarily benefit fantasy managers that chased his big-play abilities this offseason as Odunze has largely been a fantasy dud outside of the Week 4 win over the Jets in which he returned 15.4 PPR points. He remains best left on fantasy benches ahead of another difficult test against the Seahawks in Week 8.

item.title: Luther Burden caught all four targets for 130 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 7 win over the Patriots, adding seven yards on one carry.
item.description:
Luther Burden CHI Wide Receiver

Burden erupted on the scene with a 58-yard, catch-and-run reception on a crosser in the first quarter to set up a four-yard score for D’Andre Swift. He would tack on another 24 yards and his touchdown late in the second quarter to push him over the century mark in yards on an improbable touchdown reception, taking a quick screen to the house on third-and-17 with only 14 seconds remaining before the break. Burden would largely fall victim to a more reserved offensive stance after the Bears pushed their lead to 13 points on their first possession of the second half, adding just one additional reception in the final 30 minutes of play. That matters not to fantasy managers that had been waiting for a marquee performance from a player they chased up draft boards this summer. Burden appears to be heating up now further removed from the offseason injury he carried into the start of the regular season and can continue to be started as an upside WR2 ahead of a difficult matchup against the Seahawks in Week 8.

item.title: D’Andre Swift rushed 22 times for 78 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 7 win over the Patriots, adding 12 yards on four receptions.
item.description:
D'Andre Swift CHI Running Back

Swift shook off an early injury scare when he took a helmet directly to his knee to earn a season-high 26 opportunities in the absence of Kyle Monangai. This game had an entirely different feel than the previous game played without Monangai, during which Roschon Johnson was much more involved in a game the Bears held a 31-7 lead in the fourth quarter. The back-and-forth nature of Week 7 kept Swift on the field for more of the game, allowing him to return a legitimate RB1 performance on the backs of elite volume. Monangai could return as early as Week 8 considering the Bears now have 10 days until they play the Seahawks on Monday Night Football, potentially sending Swift back into the RB2 range in fantasy circles.

item.title: Caleb Williams completed 22-of-33 passes for 308 yards and two touchdowns in the Bears’ 30-24, Week 7 win over the Patriots, adding 18 yards on five carries.
item.description:
Caleb Williams CHI Quarterback

The enigmatic signal caller also took three sacks, the last of which almost placed the Bears in position to hand the keys to victory to the Patriots. Ben Johnson called a pass play on third-and-five with under two minutes to play in Patriots territory, placing another nod of support toward his franchise quarterback. Things turned dire when Williams took a sack that appeared to take the Bears out of field goal range in a six-point game, with veteran kicker Cairo Santos hitting a career-long 58-yard field goal to dispel the worries. That sequence of two plays displayed Johnson’s unrelenting trust in his players considering the 58-yard field goal was not only the longest of Santos’ 12-year career, but the third longest field goal in Soldier Field history. Either way, Williams and the Bears escaped with the victory and move to 5-2, now 1.5-games behind the Vikings for the division lead in the most competitive division in football. The Bears get a mini-bye ahead of a Week 8 meeting with the Seahawks on Monday Night Football, where Williams will remain a back-end QB1 in fantasy.

item.title: DeMario Douglas caught 3-of-4 targets for 23 yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears.
item.description:
DeMario Douglas NE Wide Receiver

The magic of the previous two games quickly evaporated for the diminutive slot receiver as Hunter Henry and Rhamondre Stevenson stepped into the primary security blanket role for Drake Maye, the latter of whom faced consistent pressure from the aggressive Dennis Allen Bears defense. Starting Douglas on a weekly basis is akin to reaching your hand into a brown paper bag found on the side of the road. It feels exhilarating at the time but you never know what you’re going to get.

item.title: A.J. Brown caught 3-of-6 targets for 48 yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears.
item.description:
A.J. Brown NE Wide Receiver

Brown has not yet clicked with his new team after going down with injury in Week 1 and spending the subsequent four games on injured reserve. He committed yet another drop against the Bears after three drops the week prior, this time on what would have been a long gain down the left sideline. Brown’s burst off the line and at the top of routes appears to remain hampered, something both the Patriots and Brown’s fantasy managers hope will remedy in short order. You can’t really sit Brown at this point, but fantasy managers have to be growing impatient of their first or second-round selection. Brown remains a teeth-gritting start ahead of a Week 8 matchup with the Dolphins.

item.title: Hunter Henry caught all seven targets for 71 yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears.
item.description:
Hunter Henry NE Tight End

Henry operated as the clear safety blanket for quarterback Drake Maye, the latter of whom was under constant duress in the face of unrelenting pressure from Dennis Allen’s Bears defense. The team was largely unable to move the football on the ground and fell into an early hole, leading to Josh McDaniels utilizing the short passing game as an extension of the run. That’s where Henry made his presence felt, although it was rookie tight end Eli Raridon that caught the touchdown at the position. Week 7 goes down as the first game with more than a modest five targets for the veteran tight end, who has quickly become a difficult weekly start in a more crowded New England pass offense. Fantasy managers might want to consider alternatives when the Patriots face the downtrodden Dolphins in Week 8.

item.title: TreVeyon Henderson rushed three times for nine yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears, adding 14 yards on two receptions.
item.description:
TreVeyon Henderson NE Running Back

Henderson continues to play second, or third, fiddle behind Rhamondre Stevenson when the Patriots are forced into “gotta have it” mode, with Stevenson the back most trusted in key situations. The Patriots fell into an early hole and were playing catch-up throughout against the Bears, something that could help to explain the lowly opportunity total for the back widely considered the more explosive of the two. Furthermore, the team continued to rotate Corey Kiner through the opportunity pecking order, placing another sizable dent in the weekly floor of Henderson. Although he could find more opportunities in a softer matchup in Week 8, he’ll be a difficult click to insert into fantasy lineups against the Dolphins.

item.title: Rhamondre Stevenson rushed six times for 22 yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears, adding 93 yards and a touchdown on five receptions.
item.description:
Rhamondre Stevenson NE Running Back

Stevenson scored one of the more improbable touchdowns you will see late in the second quarter. After taking possession with just 14 seconds remaining on the clock, Drake Maye completed an 18-yard pass to A.J. Brown to place the ball near midfield with three seconds remaining before the half. Instead of heaving the ball deep on a Hail Mary, Maye dumped the ball off to Stevenson in the flat with blockers out front. Stevenson would do the rest on his way to a 48-yard score as time expired in the second frame on a score that never really should have happened. The six carries go down as a season-low for the veteran back, although 11 opportunities handily led the team. Stevenson has not seen more than 14 carries since Week 1 and is not finding paint frequently enough to remain a consistent RB2, making him a shaky weekly start moving forward. That holds true ahead of a Week 8 meeting with the Dolphins.

item.title: Drake Maye completed 24-of-31 passes for 321 yards, two touchdown, and one interception in the Patriots’ 30-24, Week 7 loss to the Bears, adding 26 yards and a touchdown on four carries.
item.description:
Drake Maye NE Quarterback

Maye and the Patriots struggled to tame an unrelenting Chicago pass rush and were unable to move the football on the ground effectively, two cariables that led to an early deficit against the Bears. Their first half possessions went turnover on downs, three-and-out, three-and-out, touchdown, interception before a wild series to end the second quarter. Caleb Williams led a touchdown drive that left only 14 seconds on the clock. After an 18-yard completion to A.J. Brown, just three seconds remained with the ball near midfield. That’s when Maye dumped the ball off to Rhamondre Stevenson in the flat underneath deep prevent coverage, and Stevenson did the rest on a touchdown that never should have happened to bring the game to a one-possession game. Maye’s other touchdown toss was a beautiful bread-basket throw to rookie tight end Eli Raridon up the seam, adding a score on a grit-play rushing touchdown early in the second quarter. It goes down as Maye’s fourth consecutive QB1 fantasy performance after starting the season leading the league in turnovers through three weeks. The 4-3 Patriots get a mini-bye ahead of a divisional meeting against the Dolphins in Week 8, where Maye will remain an upside QB1.

item.title: Cole Kmet (knee) was carted to the locker room in the fourth quarter of Week 7 against the Patriots.
item.description:
Cole Kmet CHI Tight End

Kmet was sandwiched by two defenders on a hit in the fourth quarter and remained down on the field. He immediately grabbed at his knee as he remained on the turf. The cart was summoned and he was taken to the locker room, giving a thumbs up to the crowd as he went. Fantasy managers in deep leagues will want to track his status in the coming days, but it did not look good. Kmet managed to catch all three targets for 28 yards prior to departing.

item.title: Dalton Schultz (quad) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Dalton Schultz HOU Tight End

Correcting a previous item, Schultz ended up practicing today. He was limited, as was Brevin Jordan (foot), who evidently picked up a new injury. Schultz’s return gives him a chance to face the Giants this week. Ideally, he will upgrade to full participation tomorrow, though it is possible he gets hit with the questionable tag if he remains limited.

Source: Houston Texans

item.title: Carson Beck (back) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Carson Beck ARI Quarterback

Beck appeared on the injury report last Friday, as a limited participant. He remained limited on Wednesday and was downgraded today. Beat reporters saw him at practice briefly, but he ended up going inside with a trainer. This could help preserve Jacoby Brissett’s job security. Stay tuned.

Source: Theo Mackie

item.title: Rashid Shaheed (hip) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Rashid Shaheed SEA Wide Receiver

Shaheed will be good to go for the Seahawks’ Week 7 game against the Chiefs, barring a setback. Unfortunately, his terribly volatile performances keep him in the boom-bust FLEX tier despite four teams being on bye. For what it’s worth, this could be a fantasy-friendly game environment.

Source: Bob Condotta

item.title: Jaylen Waddle (chest) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Jaylen Waddle DEN Wide Receiver

The Broncos’ big-name offseason acquisition has totaled more than 35 yards just once all year, and now he has a chest injury. Waddle is on track to play, and he faces a beatable Cardinals pass defense this week, but he can only be treated as a FLEX starter at this time.

Source: Denver Broncos

item.title: Jonah Coleman (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Jonah Coleman DEN Running Back

Coleman is trending toward returning for the Broncos’ Week 7 game against the Cardinals. His teammate, RB Tyler Badie (thumb), remains sidelined. Coleman makes for a risky start if active, but the Broncos’ coaching staff likes him. He should be rostered in 12-team formats.

Source: Denver Broncos

item.title: Mike Washington (foot/back) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Mike Washington Jr. LV Running Back

Dang. This suggests Washington suffered one or both injuries yesterday in practice. He is firmly in the questionable camp and may have only a long shot at suiting up in Week 7 against the Rams. Without him, Ashton Jeanty should handle a solid workload. Dylan Laube could end up serving as the No. 2 running back.

Source: Adam Grosbard

item.title: Bears declared Kyle Monangai, LB T.J. Edwards, LB Jack Sanborn, OL Jordan McFadden, DT Jayden Loving, CB Nick McCloud and QB Case Keenum inactive for Week 7 against the Patriots.
item.description:
Kyle Monangai CHI Running Back

D’Andre Swift will serve as the team’s top back, while Roschon Johnson rotates in behind him. Johnson’s Week 6 fumble could result in less playing time. The Bears face the Seahawks in Week 8. Monangai was unable to practice all week. Hopefully, he returns next week and can be on the field on game day. Keenum will serve as the emergency third quarterback today.

Source: Brad Biggs

item.title: Christian Gonzalez (illness) is active for Week 7 against the Bears.
item.description:
Christian Gonzalez NE Cornerback

Gonzalez is active, but it sounds like he is not feeling great. ESPN’s Mike Reiss writes that Gonzalez “will attempt to play through” his illness. The Patriots declared DT Joshua Farmer, QB Behren Morton, G/C Ben Brown (knee), CB Karon Prunty (hamstring), CB Channing Canada (hamstring) and CB Carlton Davis III (neck) inactive for Week 7 against the Bears. Davis serves as the team’s No. 2 perimeter cornerback. Prunty and Canada are Gonzalez and Davis’ primary backups. The Bears’ passing game should play productively tonight.

Source: Mike Reiss

item.title: Brock Bowers (hamstring/calf) practiced in full on Wednesday.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

Phew. Seeing Bowers return to full participation today is heartening. The star tight end appeared on the injury report as a limited participant yesterday, leaving some questions as to when the injuries occured, and how severe they are. Ideall, he remains full tomorrow and can be started as an elite TE1 as usual against the Rams this week.

Source: Adam Grosbard

item.title: Trent McDuffie (groin) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Trent McDuffie

McDuffie, the Rams’ No. 1 cornerback, and LB Nate Landman (concussion) were both sidelined today. Both players are on the wrong side of questionable for the Rams’ Week 7 game against the Raiders.

Source: Adam Grosbard

item.title: Landon Dickerson (knee/pectoral) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Landon Dickerson PHI Guard

Eagles C Drew Kendall (knee) was also limited. Both players were listed as questionable to play in Week 6 against the Panthers. Neither player was able to suit up. Beginning the week with limited sessions is promising. The Eagles face the Cowboys on Monday night.

Source: Jeff McLane

item.title: Dallas Goedert (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Dallas Goedert PHI Tight End

Goedert missed time with a knee injury earlier this year, but he was not on the injury report last week. This could just be a maintenance day, but it is worth keeping an eye on in the lead up to the Eagles’ Monday Night Football game against the Cowboys.

Source: Jeff McLane

item.title: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

The Eagles held Smith out for multiple drives in Week 6 against the Panthers, in his first game back from a multi-week hamstring injury. He was also dealing with a toe issue. The latter injury is now behind him, and we suspect that his day off today is just a veteran maintenance day. He should be good to go for the Eagles’ Week 7 game against the Cowboys on Monday night.

Source: Jeff McLane

item.title: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Dontayvion Wicks PHI Wide Receiver

Wicks swaps out his multi-week hamstring injury for an ankle injury. He managed to play through it in Week 6 against the Panthers after meeting with the training staff. We expect him to face the Cowboys on Monday night, but he is just a boom-bust FLEX.

Source: Jeff McLane

item.title: ESPN’s Stephen Holder listed QuentonNelson and DeForest Buckner as potential trade options for the Colts.
item.description:
Quenton Nelson IND Guard

Holder writes that “trade speculation is swirling” around Buckner and notes that Nelson is in the final year of his deal, potentially providing motivation for the Colts to move him. Neither player had much to say when asked about a potential trade, but per Holder, “it is widely expected that significant organizational changes might be coming after the eventual hire of a new general manager.” Stay tuned.

Source: ESPN

item.title: ESPN’s Stephen Holder reports that several teams are interested in trading for Jonathan Taylor.
item.description:
Jonathan Taylor IND Running Back

According to Holder, multiple teams would be open to trading for Taylor, but it remains unclear whether the Colts are ready to be sellers before the trade deadline. Colts GM Chris Ballard was recently fired, and “it is widely expected that significant organizational changes might be coming” after the eventual hiring of a new general manager.

Source: ESPN

item.title: Christian Gonzalez (illness) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Bears.
item.description:
Christian Gonzalez NE Cornerback

Gonzalez has evidently come down with an illness. The Patriots will announce their inactive list in less than an hour. They are already without CB2 Carlton Davis (neck) and their top perimeter backup CBs Karon Prunty (hamstring) and Channing Canada (hamstring), plus S Craig Woodson (shoulder) is questionable to play.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Puka Nacua left practice early after suffering a calf injury on Thursday.
item.description:
Puka Nacua

Brutal. The Rams lost Davante Adams to a hamstring tendon rupture in Week 6 against the Cardinals, and now they could be without Nacua in Week 7 against the Raiders. The Rams have handled star-player injuries smartly this season. Consider Nacua highly questionable to play, and seek out a backup plan. Konata Mumpfield would serve as the de facto No. 1 wide receiver if Nacua is unable to play.

Source: Gary Klein

item.title: Nick Bosa (calf) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Nick Bosa SF Defensive Lineman

The 49ers were optimistic about Bosa’s availability for Week 7 against the Falcons, but he is firmly on the wrong side of questionable. The 49ers go on bye in Week 8. Allowing him to fully heal and return in Week 9 for their game against the Raiders could make sense.

Source: Nick Wagoner

item.title: Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

NBC Sports’ Jennifer Lee Chan reported earlier this week that Evans is expected to “miss a little time,” making his two absences unsurprising. Evans has not been formally ruled out, and he is no stranger to playing through injury, but fantasy managers should expect him to miss the 49ers’ Week 7 game against the Falcons.

Source: Nick Wagoner

item.title: Christian Kirk (calf) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Christian Kirk SF Wide Receiver

Kirk is on track to make his 2026 debut this week in the 49ers’ game against the Falcons. As strange as it sounds, Kirk has a chance to vault into the 49ers’ No. 1 wide receiver role with Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) expected to sit out this week. Kirk should be rostered in 12-team formats.

Source: Nick Wagoner

item.title: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Brian Robinson ATL Running Back

The Falcons’ No. 2 running back was limited yesterday. This series of events suggests Robinson strained his hamstring on Wednesday, putting him on the wrong side of questionable for the Falcons’ Week 6 game against the 49ers. Bijan Robinson would handle a few extra touches in Robinson’s absence. The team does not have a third running back on the active roster.

Source: Marc Raimondi

item.title: Justin Jefferson (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Justin Jefferson MIN Wide Receiver

The Vikings’ No. 1 wide receiver posted a 6/79/1 receiving line in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints. He should be feeling even better at this point, coming off a Week 6 bye. The Colts will notably be without No. 1 cornerback Sauce Gardner (calf) this weekend, making life even easier on Jefferson.

Source: Adam Caplan

item.title: T.J. Hockenson (concussion) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
T.J. Hockenson MIN Tight End

Hockenson did the same yesterday and can be safely expected to start in Week 7 against the Colts’ beatable defense. Hockenson has seemingly developed a strong connection with Kyler Murray and can be started as a fantasy football TE1 this week.

Source: Adam Caplan

item.title: Buccaneers placed Christian Rozeboom on injured reserve with a finger injury.
item.description:
Christian Rozeboom TB Linebacker

Rozeboom heads to injured reserve with five tackles and one quarterback pressure to his name. The Buccaneers correspondingly activated David Sills from injured reserve

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: Travis Kelce (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Travis Kelce KC Tight End

Kelce should be good to go for the Chiefs’ Week 7 game against the Seahawks. At 37 years old, he does not need to practice fully in order to play, though it would be nice to see him upgrade to full participation tomorrow. If active, he is a locked-in TE1.

Source: Kansas City Chiefs

item.title: Rashee Rice (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Rashee Rice KC Wide Receiver

Chiefs coach Andy Reid told reporters that Rice’s strain was only a “tweak” in his Week 4 post-game remarks. So much for that. The Chiefs will almost assuredly be without their No. 1 wide receiver against the Seahawks this week, leaving Xavier Worthy to handle the role.

Source: Kansas City Chiefs

item.title: Tyler Guyton (calf) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Thursday.
item.description:
Tyler Guyton DAL Tackle

The Cowboys’ left tackle played through a minor back issue earlier this month as well. He’s a little banged up at the moment. Whether this injury keeps him out remains to be seen. The Cowboys take on the division-rival Eagles on Monday night.

Source: Todd Archer

item.title: George Pickens (shoulder) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Thursday.
item.description:
George Pickens DAL Wide Receiver

Reliable ESPN beat reporter Todd Archer notes that Pickens has had ice on his shoulder during the Cowboys’ last two games. He does not think that this injury threatens Pickens’ Week 7 availability. Thanks, Todd. Ideally, Pickens jumps back up to full participation tomorrow, and we head into Sunday carefree. Stay tuned.

Source: Todd Archer

item.title: Dalton Schultz (quad) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Dalton Schultz HOU Tight End

Schultz is unlikely to play in Week 7 against the Giants, and now Texans TE4 Brevin Jordan (foot) appears to have suffered an injury. Jordan was added to the injury report today as a limited participant. The injuries elevate TE2 Foster Moreau to the streaming ranks for Week 7.

Source: Houston Texans

item.title: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Rashod Bateman BAL Wide Receiver

Bateman has been playing through this shoulder injury for a while, though he was forced to leave early last week. Bateman should now be expected to play, but he is only a boom-bust FLEX option with Ja’Kobi Lane now back in the lineup.

Source: Baltimore Ravens

item.title: Dylan Sampson (knee) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Dylan Sampson CLE Running Back

The Browns could get their receiving specialist back in the lineup this week, though it would be nice to see him practice fully tomorrow. Sampson injured his knee while returning a kickoff in Week 1 against the Jaguars and has been sidelined ever since.

Source: Camryn Justice

item.title: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Quinshon Judkins CLE Running Back

Yesterday, Browns coach Todd Monken said he was “optimistic” about Judkins’ Week 7 availability. He has a chance to face the Titans this week, after sitting out in Week 6 against the Ravens, but it would be great to resume practicing in full tomorrow. If active, Judkins could be limited to a run-centric role, with Sampson also technically being on track to play.

Source: Camryn Justice

item.title: Rhamondre Stevenson rushed six times for 22 yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears, adding 93 yards and a touchdown on five receptions.
item.description:
Rhamondre Stevenson NE Running Back

Stevenson scored one of the more improbable touchdowns you will see late in the second quarter. After taking possession with just 14 second remaining on the clock, Drake Maye completed an 18-yard pass to A.J. Brown to place the ball near midfield with three seconds remaining before the half.
